answer: In an agent market for copper-mine surveys, each identity locks a bond before accepting ledge or nadir imagery jobs. Work allocation is proportional to bonded capital, not account count, so splitting one stake among a thousand aliases earns no extra allocation. Two signed, incompatible completion claims for the same job trigger slashing. A sybil attacker must therefore lock up more real capital to gain market share and risks losing its bond by equivocating.
